Source: Despite some improvement noticed in developed countries, the control of these preventable diseases in African countries including Nigeria and Egypt seems insurmountable.

Source: Therefore, this study focused on assessing the knowledge and uptake of Nigerians and Egyptians towards breast self-examination (BSE) and breast and cervical cancer screening.
Luganda: Noolwekyo, okunoonyereza kuno kwassa essira ku kwekenneenya okumanya n’okwettanira kw’abantu b’omu Nigeria ne Egypt okw’okwekebera BSE n’okwekebeza kookolo w’amabeere n’ow’omumwa gwa nabaana.
Yoruba: Fún ìdí èyí, iṣẹ́ ìwádìí yìí gbájúmọ́ ṣíṣe àgbéyẹ̀wò ìmọ̀ àti ipa orílẹ̀ èdè Nàìjíríà àti Egypt lórí ìṣàyẹ̀wò-ọlọ́danni (BSE) àti Ìṣàyẹ̀wò jẹjẹrẹ ọyàn àti tí ojú ara obìnrin.
Zulu: Ngakho, lolu cwaningo lugxile ekuhloleni ulwazi kanye nokhetha ukuhlolwa kwabase-Nigerai kanye naseGibhithe mayelana nokuzihlola amabele (i-BSE) kanye nokuhlolela umdlavuza webele kanye nowomlomo wesibeletho.
Hausa: Don haka, wannan binciken ya mayar da hankali ne a kan tantance ilimi da ɗaukar nauyin ‘yan Nijeriya da Misirawa a kan bincika nono da kai (BSE) da tantance cutar kansar nono da ta mara.
